# The yen and the euro against interest-rate gaps: one weekly test

*Generated by `python3 bin/fx_rate_gap.py build`; do not edit by hand. Specification: `_research/2026-10-18-FX-Rate-Gap-Weekly-Spec.md`. Data: U.S. Department of the Treasury (home.treasury.gov) retrieved 2026-10-18; Ministry of Finance Japan (www.mof.go.jp) retrieved 2026-10-18; European Central Bank (data-api.ecb.europa.eu) retrieved 2026-10-18; Bank for International Settlements (stats.bis.org) retrieved 2026-10-18; Deutsche Bundesbank (api.statistiken.bundesbank.de) retrieved 2026-10-18.*

## In five sentences

1. We asked whether, after the Bank of Japan changed its policy framework on 19 March 2024, the yen's weekly moves against the US dollar went together with weekly changes in the gap between the US and Japanese 2-year government bond yields, and how much of the yen's total move over those weeks that gap-change term accounts for.
2. For each week we measured the change in the natural log of the yen price of a dollar and the change in the 2-year gap (US minus Japan, in percentage points), and drew the best straight line, with a constant, through those weekly pairs.
3. The weeks run from the one ending 29 March 2024 to the one ending 18 September 2026: 130 weekly changes, of which 118 remain after dropping 10 weeks that overlap a Japanese intervention and 2 weeks in which a yield quote was stale.
4. The one test is whether the slope of that line differs from zero (two-sided, 5%, HC3 standard errors), and a decision rule fixed before any exchange rate was read then asks what share of the yen's cumulative move over the kept weeks the fitted gap-change term accounts for.
5. It cannot show that rates, flows, positions or intervention made the yen move, it says nothing about the intervention weeks themselves, and a short sample can miss an effect that is there.

## A worked example

Take the first kept week, the one ending 29 March 2024 (the exchange rate is the BIS daily rate on 2024-03-28, equal to the ECB reference cross; the change runs from the rate on 2024-03-22). The log of yen per dollar changed by -0.000663 (about -0.07%) and the 2-year gap changed by -0.070 percentage points. The fitted slope for the whole sample is beta = 0.058331, so the gap-change term for that week is beta x gap change = 0.058331 x -0.070 = -0.004083. The week adds -0.000663 to S, the sum of the yen's log changes over the kept weeks, and -0.004083 to F, the sum of the fitted gap-change terms. Over all 118 kept weeks S = 0.1269 and F = -0.0522, so phi = F / S is -0.4113.

## Four definitions

- **Log change.** The natural log of this week's price divided by last week's; 0.01 is about 1%.
- **Gap.** The US yield minus the foreign yield, in percentage points; a wider gap and a stronger dollar both push the series up, so the slope is expected to be positive.
- **HC3.** Standard errors that let each week have its own variance and damp the weight of influential weeks.
- **Placebo.** The same regression with the gap series slid out of line in time (by 13 to n-13 weeks, wrapping round), to see how large the slope looks by chance.

This build is one test plus description: the regression of section 3.6 of the specification on the 2-year gap, in sample P, is the only confirmatory test. Every other row (the 10-year gap, the joint regression, the other samples, every euro row) is description. `regressions.csv` prints k = 48 descriptive rows in its second line; a reader who treats them as tests must use 0.05 / k.

## Commands

```
python3 bin/fx_rate_gap.py selftest   # synthetic data, no network: guards G1-G21 of the spec plus X1-X6 added by the builder; every mutant must be caught
python3 bin/fx_rate_gap.py fetch      # the only network command: 19 requests, 2 s apart; a refusal writes data/vintages/fx_rate_gap/STOP
python3 bin/fx_rate_gap.py build      # offline: writes the files in this folder; a second run is byte-identical
```

The raw downloads and the weekly panel stay in `data/vintages/fx_rate_gap/`, which `.gitignore` keeps out of the repository, because the panel would let a reader rebuild yield levels. This folder holds only statistics, the decision, a few pinned values, the intervention list, the checks and the fetch log.

## When each yield is observed (the time-zone rule)

A week runs Monday to Friday; its exchange rate is the BIS daily rate on the last day of the week with an ECB reference rate (normally the Friday). No yield is observed after that rate: Japan's is the MoF yield on that day or the last earlier one (15:00 Tokyo, about 06:00 GMT), and the US and euro-area yields are the last observations strictly before it (normally Thursday's close). The same-Friday US yield, observed about seven hours after the exchange rate, is kept only as a fragility check (variant c). What remains: the exchange-rate change runs from fix to fix, while the US and euro legs run from Thursday close to Thursday close, so news in Friday's Asian and London hours enters this week's exchange rate but next week's yield change.

## The denominator of phi and two identities

S is the sum of the yen's log changes over the **kept** weeks only. The sum over all 130 weeks of P, S_all = 0.042696, is never the denominator; S_all = S + S_dropped (0.042696 = 0.126917 + -0.084221) holds by construction. Because the residuals of a regression with a constant sum to zero, S = n x alpha + F (0.126917 = 0.179123 + -0.052206): the intercept absorbs any level or carry channel, so a share phi near zero does not mean the gap's level is irrelevant.

## What to expect (written before the run)

X, the sum of the 2-year gap changes over the kept weeks, is negative over P (the gap narrowed). With a positive slope, phi >= 0.50 therefore needs S < 0: the yen must have strengthened, in dollar terms, over the kept weeks. The power arithmetic makes INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered) the expected outcome; in that case the build's value is the descriptive table, not a verdict.

## Why the 2-year gap (a forking path, disclosed)

The choice of the 2-year gap rather than the slope gap was made after the specification's author had seen how the candidate regressors moved over P: the four end-point yields and the totals of the three candidate gaps (+0.044, -1.593 and -1.549 percentage points over all 130 weeks of P). No exchange rate was used. A primary regressor chosen with knowledge of the regressors' own path is one fork of the garden, even when the outcome is unseen. The slope-gap regression stays in every output as the SEPARATE row, and the full-sample row is printed beside the primary every time.

## What this can and cannot say

It can say whether, in non-intervention weeks from 29 March 2024 to 18 September 2026, the yen moved with the 2-year gap, at what rate, and whether the weekly 2-year-gap-change term accounts for at least half, or for less than a quarter, of the yen's cumulative log change over those weeks, or points the other way. That is association: the coefficient is MEASURED (observed on the stated data, and can be wrong), and the share, given the coefficient, is an IDENTITY (true by construction, so it carries no information beyond its inputs). It cannot say that rates, flows, positions or intervention moved anything; anything about the intervention weeks, which are dropped; or anything about real yields, policy rates or forecasting. It cannot say that rates do not matter if the power gate fails. The post-March-2024 sample was dated after the 2024-26 path had been tabulated, so the primary is not a blind test.

A move in an intervention week is not attributed to the intervention by `event_weeks.csv`; its `fitted_term` column uses the sample-P coefficient for every listed week.

## What the registered run printed

Run label `csv_through_2026-06-30_blocks_1`. Verdict of record: **WEEKLY 2Y-GAP TERM POINTS THE OTHER WAY**. n = 118; beta = 0.058331 (HC3 SE 0.012514, p <0.0001; Newey-West SE 0.013544, p <0.0001); S = 0.126917, X = -0.895000 pp, F = -0.052206; phi = -0.4113 (interval -0.5843 to -0.2384); placebo SD 0.012610 over 93 shifts; half-width of the phi interval 0.1743 (gate PASS).

The 'what to expect' paragraph above anticipated INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered); that did not happen, because the gate was passed: the half-width of the phi interval is 0.174 against the limit 0.25. The gate needs |S| above about 0.08 to 0.11 (the specification's ex-ante arithmetic), and S = 0.127 is above it. In plain words: over the 118 kept weeks the 2-year gap narrowed by 0.9 percentage points, which on the weekly slope goes with a stronger yen (-5.2% in log terms), while the yen weakened by 12.7% (log terms). The yen's move over those weeks sits in the constant term (n x alpha = 0.179), not in the gap term. This describes co-movement; it does not show what moved the yen.

The same regression on the full sample (436 weeks): beta = 0.056682 (HC3 SE 0.005209). The separate slope-gap row: beta = -0.045630 (p 0.0203), phi = 0.1079; the sum of the slope-gap changes over the 118 kept weeks is -0.300 pp (+0.044 pp is the sum over all 130 weeks of P), so phi_s is near zero by construction.

Every count matches the reviewer's (specification 3.5): FULL 455 weeks (436 kept), W1 209 (205), W2 104 (101), W3 142 (130), P 130 (118).

## Data notes (what the checks found in the sources)

- **ECB dates left out of the euro leg.** 2022-06-23: the Svensson parameters reproduce the published 2- and 10-year zero yields only to 1.0e-02 (tolerance 1e-6); 2021-12-14: the parameter set is incomplete in the file. Both lie outside the yen regressions, which use no ECB yield; the euro rows, which are description, use the previous ECB date for the week ending 2022-06-24.
- **The ECB's published continuous-coupon par yields before 2024.** Recomputed from the parameters they agree to 1e-10 from 1 January 2024 and differ before it (largest gap 4.2e-03; 276 of 314 weekly dates above the spec's 1e-4). The zero yields agree on every date but the one named above, and the semiannual par yield used in the euro gap needs only the zero curve, so the euro gap does not depend on the published par yields.

## Appendix: the decision rule (specification section 4, summarised)

Written on 18 October 2026, before any exchange-rate series or coefficient was computed. Quantities, in sample P with the kept weeks: S is the sum of dln(yen per dollar); X is the sum of the 2-year gap changes; F = beta x X; phi = F / S (left blank if |S| <= 0.01). The phi interval is (beta -/+ 1.959964 SE) x X / S with the endpoints sorted. The standard errors: the power gate uses max(placebo SD, SE_HC3); the primary's intervals and verdict use SE_HC3; variant (a) uses SE_NW4 for its interval and max(placebo SD, SE_NW4) for its printed gate; variants (b) and (c) use their own SE_HC3 and their own placebo.

Power gate (computed before beta is read): the placebo re-estimates beta on every circular shift of the kept gap series by 13 ... n-13 weeks (n - 25 shifts). If 1.959964 x SE_gate x |X| / |S| exceeds 0.25 the design is underpowered and the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, whatever beta is.

Classes, with no gate inside them: UNCLASSIFIED if |S| <= 0.01 or |X| < 0.5 pp; AT LEAST HALF if beta > 0, p < 0.05, phi >= 0.50 and the lower end of the phi interval > 0.25; POINTS THE OTHER WAY if the upper end < 0; LESS THAN A QUARTER if 0 <= the upper end < 0.25; otherwise UNCLASSIFIED. The verdict of record is INCONCLUSIVE if |S| <= 0.01, |X| < 0.5 pp or the primary's gate fails; otherwise each of three variants is classified by its own phi and interval without a gate, (a) Newey-West lag 4, (b) the intervention weeks restored (stale weeks stay out), (c) the same-calendar-Friday US leg, and the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE (fragile) if any variant's class differs from the primary's; otherwise it is the primary's class. The 0.25 and 0.50 marks, the 0.5 pp floor, lag 4 and the 13-week placebo floor are pre-commitments, not estimates. The euro rows have no verdict.
